prompt: Summarize the following annual report excerpt into exactly 5 bullet points for an executive audience.
input_text:
Alpenwerk Logistics AG – Annual Report 2025 (excerpt, fictional company)

Net revenue rose 8% to CHF 412 million, driven mainly by growth in contract logistics for pharmaceutical clients. Operating margin (EBIT) improved from 6.1% to 7.4% as the new automated warehouse in Basel reached full capacity in Q2. The road freight division, however, saw revenue fall 3% due to lower volumes from the automotive sector and rising driver wages.
The company invested CHF 38 million, of which CHF 22 million went into warehouse automation and CHF 9 million into a new transport management system scheduled to go live in mid-2026. Headcount grew from 2,150 to 2,240 employees. CO2 emissions per tonne-kilometre were reduced by 11% thanks to 40 new electric trucks.
For 2026, management expects revenue growth of 4–6% and plans to enter the Austrian market through a small acquisition. The board proposes a dividend of CHF 2.40 per share (prior year: CHF 2.10).
reference: Must cover: (1) revenue +8% to CHF 412m, driven by pharma contract logistics; (2) EBIT margin up from 6.1% to 7.4% due to Basel automated warehouse; (3) road freight revenue down 3% (automotive volumes, driver wages); (4) CHF 38m investment incl. automation and new TMS (go-live mid-2026); (5) outlook 4–6% growth, Austria entry via acquisition, dividend CHF 2.40. Exactly 5 bullets, no invented figures.

prompt: Condense the following article into a brief of no more than 60 words for a busy executive.
input_text:
Mid-sized European manufacturers are increasingly experimenting with generative AI, but few have moved beyond pilots. A recent survey of 300 companies in Germany, Austria and Switzerland found that 62% had tested at least one generative AI tool in the past year, yet only 14% had deployed one in a production process. The most common pilots were in customer service, internal document search and drafting of technical documentation.
Respondents named three main barriers: unclear return on investment (cited by 58%), concerns about data protection and where data is stored (51%), and a lack of in-house skills (47%). Companies that had moved to production typically had a dedicated budget, a named executive sponsor and clear rules on which data could be used with AI tools.
Analysts expect the gap between pilots and production to narrow over the next two years as vendors offer more European hosting options and as early adopters publish measurable results. However, they warn that firms without a governance framework risk "pilot fatigue", where repeated experiments fail to deliver value and internal support fades.
(fictional article)
reference: Must convey: many DACH manufacturers pilot GenAI (62%) but few in production (14%); main barriers are unclear ROI, data protection/hosting, skills; success factors are budget, executive sponsor, data rules; outlook: gap expected to narrow, risk of pilot fatigue without governance. Max 60 words (hard check).

prompt: Identify the single most important flawed assumption in this business case and explain why it matters.
input_text:
Business case: AI chatbot for customer service (fictional)
- Today, 40 agents handle 200,000 customer inquiries per year.
- The chatbot will be launched on 1 January and will handle 100% of inquiries from day one.
- Therefore all 40 agent positions can be removed in year 1, saving CHF 3.2 million.
- Chatbot licence and maintenance cost: CHF 400,000 per year.
- Net saving year 1: CHF 2.8 million.
reference: Flawed assumption: the chatbot will handle 100% of inquiries from day one. In reality, chatbots resolve only a share of inquiries, adoption ramps up over time, and complex/escalated cases still need human agents. This makes the CHF 3.2m saving and removal of all 40 agents unrealistic; savings must be phased and partial. (Also acceptable as secondary: ignores implementation/change costs.)
